newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Swedish Riksbank not seen raising repo til 98.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swedish Riksbank not seen raising repo til 98.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, confirmed on Thursday in its quartely inflation report that further repo rate cuts are out of the question and analysts do not see any rate hikes until 1998.

The bank repeated in the report that it had no intention of changing the repo, its key interest rate, which it cut to 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent last year. It has not altered the rate since December 17.
"The Riksbank confirms that monetary policy is well balanced and that inflation remains low," it said.
Its other key interest rates, the deposit and lending rates, are currently at 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent.

"The Riksbank will hold off on moving the repo," Bengt Hansson, senior economist at Handelsbanken, told Reuters. "Repo rate cuts are out of the question and the Riksbank does not signal any rate hikes yet."
"Next step will be a rate hike which I think will come at the start of 1998," Anders Hahnel, economist at Aragon brokerage, said. Hansson and other economists agreed.

The Riksbank said the outlook for low inflation was largely unchanged but lifted its consumer price index (CPI) forecasts made in March to about one percent in 1997 and two percent for 1998 from 0.5 percent and under two percent, respectively.

"This is mainly due to the recent months' weakening of the exchange rate but it also has to do with Statistics Sweden's revised calculations of the CPI item 'house mortgage interest costs'," the Riksbank said in the report.
The crown has weakened six percent to 4.4865 against the mark from 4.2290 in October last year and Statistics Sweden has changed its CPI to include cost for home owners renewing their loans.
The Riksbank repeated that the crown was undervalued and and saw it strengthening.
"Studies carried out by the Riksbank show that the crown is currently undervalued in the longterm fundamental sense," the Riksbank said.

It saw the crown appreciating from its current level of around 122 on the trade weighted TCW index. The bank has previously suggested that a level between 109 and 118 in real terms on the TCW would be appropriate.
The Riksbank saw the underlying rate of inflation in 1997 and 1998 at 1.5-2.0 percent, in line with its target of two percent inflation with an allowed deviation of one percentage point.
"This looks fairly neutral for the market," Peter Lindquist, economist at HSBC."Midland, said. "The inflation forecast is in line with target."
The Riksbank said the falling inflation trend had ended but left its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) estimates unchanged at a two percent rise in 1997 and three percent in 1998.
"Inflationary pressure in the Swedish economy is still limited but the latest developments show that the trend of falling inflation has probably ended," the central bank said.
"The output gap is not expected to close in the coming two years," the Riksbank said.
